_comment: Rounds whose `skills-check` line in logs/driver.log named a checker as COULD NOT RUN. Read by harness/driver_health.py:unacknowledged_broken_checker_rounds, asserted by harness/tests/test_driver_health.py. Same idiom as state/known-escalated-diffs.json: an adjudicated finding stays visible and stays quiet, and a NEW instance is loud. Round 451 (harness A) created this because the corpus check cannot observe itself -- test_corpus_check.py::TestLiveCorpus::test_every_checker_actually_ran runs INSIDE the `unit_tests` checker, so the re-entry guard drops `unit_tests` from checks() and the test asserts assertNotIn('unit_tests', ...) to say so. The one test whose job is to catch a checker that stopped running is structurally blind to the only checker that stopped running. This registry plus driver.log is the eye that sits outside the guard.
_why: All five are `unit_tests`, and all five are ONE cause, measured in round 451 rather than guessed: the suite takes 162.34s solo on this idle 1-core box against a 600s budget, and the driver runs FOUR pytest suites concurrently (run_driver.sh HEALTH_PID/WHENCE_PID/SKILLS_PID/NUC_PID) on `nproc` 1, which round 435 next-step 8 measured at roughly 3x. 162.3 x ~3.7 = ~600, so the checker crossed its budget by growth rather than by breaking. Round 451 removed 71s of that 162s (the four live-corpus tests in test_corpus_check.py each re-ran the whole 9-checker sweep; they now share one) and made the timeout branch report what the run salvaged instead of nothing.
_round_487_why: Rounds 483, 485 and 486 are ONE cause and it is not the one the first five were. Round 487 (harness A) timed the exact `unit_tests` argv ALONE on this box -- 183.92 s, 1074 tests, receipt at state/harness/round-487/unit-tests-solo.json -- against the 600 s budget it was killed at. The checker was never doing 600 s of work. run_driver.sh backgrounds FOUR pytest suites (HEALTH/WHENCE/SKILLS/NUC PIDs) on a box where nproc is 1, so a fair share is a quarter core and 4 x 183.92 = 735.7 s is the EXPECTED contended runtime -- over budget with no growth in the workload at all. Round 451's entry above derived a ~3.7x factor from the crossing and said out loud that it was derived rather than measured; 601/183.92 = 3.27x is the direct measurement, and it is a floor because all three observations are the kill and not a completion. THE FIX IS IN THE CODE, NOT IN THIS LIST: corpus_check.CHECK_TIMEOUT_S['unit_tests'] is now ceil(solo x DRIVER_CONCURRENT_SUITES x BUDGET_MARGIN) = 1104 s, with test_corpus_check.py::TestDerivedBudget re-deriving each factor from its source (the measurement file; a count of `_PID=$!` in run_driver.sh), so a fifth concurrent suite expires the constant instead of buying three more rounds of COULD NOT RUN.
_round_487_what_was_hidden: These three rounds were not merely uninformative -- they were hiding five real failing tests. logs/corpus-evidence/round-486/unit_tests.out is a pytest progress bar with FIVE `F`s in it, and round 487 reproduced all five solo at HEAD: test_check_round_recorded.py::test_live_registry_is_well_formed_and_every_entry_is_load_bearing, three in test_carryforward_check.py::{TestLiveCorpus x2, TestAnchorsOnTheLiveLedger}, and test_corpus_check.py::TestLiveCorpus::test_live_corpus_is_clean (carryforward K001/K002/K003). Round 451's salvage could not see them: it parses partial output with FINDING_RE, an `ERROR H001` alphabet, and a pytest progress bar answers in `.` and `F`. Over the whole of logs/driver.log, EIGHT `COULD NOT RUN: unit_tests` lines carry ZERO parsed codes between them. corpus_check.pytest_partial + partial_clause now put `; partial: unit_tests 1020 seen/5 failed` on the line run_driver.sh copies into the log, and driver_health.broken_checker_report is what prints it back when this registry does not acknowledge a round. The five failures themselves are skills(B) and session-inheritance-audit work and are reported, not fixed, by harness(A) -- see knowledge/round-487-*.md.
_expiry: This entry acknowledges these FIVE round numbers and nothing else. A sixth round reporting COULD NOT RUN is unacknowledged by construction and turns test_driver_health.py::TestBrokenCheckerHistory red. Do not add a round number here to silence a red test -- add it only with a sentence saying what was adjudicated, as these five have.
_round_451_note: The 91s figure this round leaves behind is a SOLO measurement and the contention factor it is multiplied by (~3.7) is DERIVED from the 600s crossing, not measured directly. The honest next step is to measure the same suite under the driver's own four-way concurrency, which needs a round willing to spend ~15 minutes of wall clock doing nothing else. Until then 91s x ~3.7 = ~337s is an estimate with one measured half.
